findings.item: THE D17 SWITCH REQUIREMENT -- 'turn-off-able WITHOUT EDITING CODE'
findings.detail: NOT MET, ONLY APPROXIMATED -- and the file says so itself, which is the difference between a shortfall and a misrepresentation. D17 (.rework/DECISIONS.md:445-447) is explicit: 'the refusal must be turn-off-able without editing code ... A refusal that can only be withdrawn by reverting a commit fails the instruction.' REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT and REFUSE_INEXACT_INT are module constants: flipping either is a source edit, there is no SPINE_REFUSE_* name, they take no census row and no row in the generated lever document, and an operator holding only a shell cannot reach them. lever.py's own banner (lines 84-89) states exactly that, and .rework/DECISIONS.md:531-534 records it as 'a deliberate shortfall against D17's second sentence, not an oversight'. ONE THING IS OVERSTATED: lever.py:57 calls the module constant 'the shape .rework/DECISIONS.md D17 settled on'. D17 weighed THREE carriers -- one RUN-owned switch, one lever per package, no lever -- and a module constant is not among them; what D17 settled was the REQUIREMENT, which this carrier fails. The honest phrasing is 'the shape src/ckpt/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD landed on under D17', which is what the next line already says. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: flipping the constant in-process works only if it is done BEFORE the packages' levers.py modules are imported, because the declaration-time half of the rule runs inside Lever.__init__ at import. An operator editing the file gets both halves; an operator monkeypatching after import gets only the coerce half.

findings.item: AN UNTRIPPABLE GUARD IN src/spine/lever.py THAT NOBODY REPORTED AND O15 CANNOT SEE: Config._wire's collision check
findings.detail: src/spine/lever.py::Config._wire carries two refusals in this order: (1) `if not name.startswith('d_')` and (2) `if name in self._vals` -> 'wire {name!r} collides with a declared lever of the same name'. The second CAN NEVER FIRE through any door the tree uses. To reach it a name must be BOTH d_-prefixed (or refusal 1 fires first) AND a declared lever -- and src/spine/lever.py::Lever.__set_name__ refuses any lever whose field name starts with 'd_'. The two populations are disjoint by construction, so _vals can never contain a d_ key, and I verified that directly: from_env's keys contain no d_ name, and the only way I could trip the guard at all was by hand-building Config(W, {'d_x': 999}, {}) -- a constructor call nothing in src/ makes. The comment directly above it claims the opposite and cites a reproduction: 'BOTH ENDS OF THE COLLISION. Lever.__set_name__ refuses a d_-named lever; this refuses a wire landing on a name a lever already holds. Without the pair, __getattr__ resolves _vals before _wired and the LEVER silently wins -- reproduced: a wire wrote 200000, the reader saw 999.' The pair is not two ends of one collision; the first end makes the second unreachable. This is this repository's most-recorded defect family (the survey's 60 untrippable-guard records) sitting inside the file that defines the refusal idiom, with a comment asserting it is live. git log -S shows both halves landed in the same commit (1322888), so it has been untrippable since it was written and PREDATES this run -- it is not a regression introduced here, but it is in the file under audit and no audit has reported it. NO CODE EDIT IS NEEDED to green anything (the suite is green); the honest repair is the DID IT FIRE discipline this tree already has -- mark the second clause UNREACHABLE and say by what, or delete it.

findings.detail: lever.py:316-320 -- 'three already refused at both ends by hand in src/opt/api.py::build (OPT_LR_DECAY, OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC, OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP) ... src/opt/api.py::build already accepts OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 BY NAME.' lever.py:326-329 -- 'src/opt/api.py::build refuses `lr <= 0.0` (open low), `not 0.0 <= min_frac < 1.0` (half-open) and `not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0` (closed).' AT HEAD src/opt/api.py::build CONTAINS NO CLAUSE NAMING lr_decay OR lr_restart_damp. Commit 2fd3b22 retired `damp > 1.0`, `damp < 0.0` and `not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0` into the two declarations, and opt/api.py:874-878 says so in as many words. The nine surviving `if`s in build() are lr<=0.0, weight_decay<0.0, not 0.0<=min_frac<1.0, warmup_asked<0, wavelength_asked<0, n_accum<1, n_batch_windows<1, grad_clip<0.0, unknown-group. So the one lever whose closed-at-both-ends treatment is the CENTRAL JUSTIFICATION for the closed-interval ruling -- 'src/opt/api.py::build already accepts OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 BY NAME' -- no longer has a by-name clause at all; 1.0 is accepted by the domain the ruling produced, which makes the argument circular where it reads as independent. lever.py was last edited at 6bbddc2 and the retirement landed at 2fd3b22, so this was true when written and false two commits later, with nothing in the tree noticing. O13 opens `src/opt/api.py::build`, finds `def build(opt: Config, ...)` at line 605 and passes -- which is exactly the wrong-but-existing-symbol case the brief says O13 cannot catch. EXACT REPAIR (no mechanism weakened, prose only): in lever.py:316-320 replace 'three already refused at both ends by hand in src/opt/api.py::build (OPT_LR_DECAY, OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC, OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP)' with 'three that src/opt/api.py::build refused at both ends by hand until 2026-09-14 (OPT_LR_DECAY and OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP, both now retired into domain=(0.0, 1.0) on opt/levers.py::OPTLevers; OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC, whose half-open chain survives)', and replace 'src/opt/api.py::build already accepts OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 BY NAME' with 'src/opt/api.py::build accepted OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 by name at the time this was decided, in the clause opt/api.py:878 records retiring'. In lever.py:326-329 drop '`not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0` (closed)' from the list of clauses build() refuses, or requalify it as retired; src/lm/api.py::resolve's `not 0.0 <= dropout < 1.0` at line 250 IS still there and that half of the sentence stands.

unfinished.title: A Lever object declared on two classes is refused with a message about DEFAULTS
unfinished.reason: owner file, read-only for me; low severity
unfinished.detail: `class A(LeverSet): x = lv` then `class B(LeverSet): y = lv` raises (wrapped in RuntimeError) 'x' is declared; a lever's default cannot be rewritten at runtime -- from Lever.__setattr__, because __set_name__ writes self.name. The problem is a second declaration of one Lever, not a default rewrite, and a reader given that message will look for the wrong thing. It also qualifies the module header's 'Ownership is now read from the OWNER at use time, so there is no per-object state to corrupt': self.name IS per-object state; what saves it is that a second write is refused. I verified the header's actual documented defect is fixed -- Base.env_names() stays {'QE_X'} after a subclass with a different PREFIX is declared.
